question: Why must the electric field at the surface of a charged conductor be normal to the surface under electrostatic conditions? Justify your answer.

options.A: The surface electric field must be tangential so that charges remain distributed over the surface
options.B: The electric field at a conductor surface is zero in all directions
options.C: A tangential component would move free charges along the surface, contradicting electrostatic equilibrium; hence the field is normal to the surface
options.D: The electric field is normal only because a conductor has no charges on its surface
